text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Robots will mean better working lives for people in the future.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘In the future we will work shorter hours.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Identify one value judgement from Source 4. Explain why you think it is a value judgement.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Knut’s or Saga’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
Your government is considering different actions to improve employment for local people. The
following actions are being considered:
• closing the pay gap between low and high paid workers
• increasing the funding of research into science and new technology
• spending more on education and training of employees to improve skills.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
